root_cause.text: `ceph_mdsc_build_path()` in `fs/ceph/mds_client.c` allocates a temporary `path` buffer with `__getname()` but on several error exits returns without freeing it via `__putname()`, causing a memory leak when ownership is not transferred to `path_info.path`.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `__putname(path);` before each failing `return ERR_PTR(...)` path in `ceph_mdsc_build_path()`—specifically after `ceph_get_inode_path(...)`/`ceph_encode_encrypted_dname()` errors and before `-ENAMETOOLONG`—and the commit message states these were “error code paths that did not free the `path` pointer obtained by `__getname()`.”

intent_record.how: This ensures the allocated `path` buffer is released when path construction fails, preventing a memory leak on this failure path.

bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit 550f7ca98ee028a606aa75705a7e77b1bd11720f
Author: Max Kellermann <max.kellermann@ionos.com>
Date:   Mon Nov 18 23:28:28 2024 +0100

    ceph: give up on paths longer than PATH_MAX
    
    If the full path to be built by ceph_mdsc_build_path() happens to be
    longer than PATH_MAX, then this function will enter an endless (retry)
    loop, effectively blocking the whole task.  Most of the machine
    becomes unusable, making this a very simple and effective DoS
    vulnerability.
bic_trace_step.reason: The shown code no longer contains the vulnerable retry/loop behavior or the leak-prone error path described in the root cause. In the old logic, the `pos < 0` branch would log a warning and `goto retry;`, but here that branch has been replaced with `return ERR_PTR(-ENAMETOOLONG);` after the comment: `The path is longer than PATH_MAX and this function cannot ever succeed.` This means the function now fails immediately instead of looping. The specific memory-leak issue from returning without `__putname()` is not visible in this snippet, and the relevant error path shown here does not demonstrate the leak-prone construct. The fix for the long-path case is already present in this commit.
